newsitem.title: UK: Cuba features in new sugar freight inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Cuba features in new sugar freight inquiry.

text.p: Cuba dominated the thin amount of new quoted business on London's sugar freight market on Wednesday with the Black Sea as destination, shipbrokers said.
Market talk has suggested Cuba could be retaining some of its raw sugar as physical prices firm before Brazil returns as an exporter with its centre-south crop.
"We're still expecting cargoes for end-May which is quite late and it will be interesting to see if it goes to end-June," said one shipbroker.
Of the day's new business, Louis Dreyfus quoted for 20/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to the Black Sea for May 5/10 and Alpine was in for 22,000 tonnes on the same run for May 10/15.
CSR entered the market with a new order for 20,000 tonnes in bulk from Queensland to Cigading for May 5/15.
In other news, around 140,000 tonnes of raw sugar is held up at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossisk because of bad weather and a lack of rail wagons needed to transport the sugar inland.
Some five sugar vessels are thought to be at the port and unable to unload at full capacity.
Moscow sources said they expected Russian raw sugar imports to rise sharply over the next two months, partly because material held up at the port would start to arrive at Russian refineries.
